title: Toolbox portal manifest (v1alpha1)
description: The v1 configuration contract (docs/v1-spec.md §5). Produced by hand in YAML/JSON or printed by the TypeScript builder. The server refuses any configuration that does not come from a manifest (D2).

policies.description: Named values readable from CEL as policy.<name>.

tracks.description: Long-term focus programs that group scorecards and campaigns (D01M7Y11G0YZT23W26Z9D3XW68Y).

kindGroups.description: Named groups of kinds that readers think of together (the docs, the code, the CI). Reports list the catalog group by group; a kind is in at most one group, and kinds in none are listed last.

waivers.description: Accepted failures. Each cites a decision and names one rule on one entity (D01M7Y5VWNAWB8K1DNMY31KQPQ0).

rubrics.description: Rubrics coding agents use to assess entities (docs/design/scorecards-for-scorecards.md §6). Assessments are data: committed files or ingested records, read by scorecards.

subject.description: The entity field that versions what is assessed (default `hash`). An assessment whose `subjectHash` differs from the entity's value is stale.

tools.description: Upstream tools the portal's connectors and rules need (D90, D01M800DHD0Z1RTPH7CM46GZS3B). Toolbox doesn't download them: `toolbox doctor` checks each pin, `toolbox tools config --for mise|aqua|pypi` prints an installer's input, and `toolbox tools install --via` runs the installer.

version.description: The exact version required, as the tool prints it.

mise.description: The mise tool id, e.g. aqua:rhysd/actionlint or pipx:zizmor (the same as install.mise).

install.description: The tool's id for each installer: Toolbox derives the installer's input from `version` and runs it. Declare any you support; none is required.

mise.description: mise tool id (any backend), e.g. aqua:rhysd/actionlint.

pypi.description: PyPI package, installed by uv, pipx or pip, e.g. zizmor.

forges.description: The code hosts this portal reaches beyond plain git (docs/design/forges.md): where a `change` opens its review, where a `gitlab-pipeline` executor dispatches, and, unless the entry names a ci: host, where a child with `runner: {type: ci}` runs. A git URL is on the forge whose `url` it starts with, or whose host an SSH URL names. `https://github.com` and `https://gitlab.com` need no entry; any other host is plain git until listed here.

url.description: The forge's web URL, e.g. https://gitlab.acme.dev.

type.description: The forge's driver: github (github.com, Enterprise Server) or gitlab (gitlab.com, self-managed CE and EE). Required unless url is https://github.com or https://gitlab.com.

api.description: The API base (default: https://api.github.com for github.com, <url>/api/v3 for Enterprise Server, <url>/api/v4 for GitLab).

token.description: The environment variable holding the API token (default GITHUB_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN). Toolbox's HTTP client reads it; no action's process gets it.

projects.description: Project paths a parent may dispatch CI to, `*` matching within one path segment (acme/* matches acme/pay, not acme/platform/pay). Default: the children this portal lists on the forge.

identity.description: A checkout of this portal takes who you are from your own token on this forge, not from --as: toolbox run asks the forge who owns the token in --identity-token-file or TOOLBOX_IDENTITY_TOKEN, and refuses to request, approve or reject without one. At most one forge sets it. Default false.

ci.description: The ci: host that runs runner: {type: ci} children on this forge, or none (they run no CI for this portal). Default: the forge's own CI (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, with this entry's api and token).

The CI systems this portal starts runs on, declared apart from the forges that host the code (docs/design/forges.md §4.7). A forge's entry points its children at one (forges[].ci); a github-workflow or gitlab-pipeline executor may take its endpoint and token from one (executor.ci). A child portal never names one.

name.description: What forges[].ci and executor.ci call it. Not none.

type.description: github-actions (workflow_dispatch, run tracked by id, record from the toolbox-run artifact), gitlab-ci (a pipeline with typed inputs, record from the toolbox job's artifact), or http: a service that speaks the executor protocol (run, status, cancel) and bridges to any other CI; its result's outputs.record is the child's run record.

url.description: github-actions and gitlab-ci: the web URL (default https://github.com or https://gitlab.com). http: the service's endpoint (required).

api.description: github-actions and gitlab-ci: the API base (default as for forges:).

token.description: The environment variable holding the token (default GITHUB_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN; http: none sent unless named, as a bearer token).

project.description: Where a forge project's CI runs on this host; {project} is the project's path on its forge (default {project}). A GitLab project that mirrors GitHub repositories might be mirrors/{project}.

projects.description: Projects on this host (after mapping) a parent may start runs in, `*` matching within one path segment. Default: any the forges that point here admit.

include.description: Source-only (D54, D89): globs of further YAML files, or packages `{package, with}` (a directory or github:owner/repo[/subdir]@version, with typed parameters), merged by `toolbox build`. Never present in the canonical manifest.

federation.description: Federated actions (docs/design/federated-actions.md): for a parent, the kind whose entities are child portals, whose declared actions it offers and dispatches to them, and the runners it owns; for a child, how a parent may reach it and whose approvals it accepts.

portals.description: The kind whose entities are child portals (workspace `portal` records: path, actions, results). Default `Portal` when `children` is set.

children.description: A parent's child portals, by git repository. Each is cloned into the state directory and kept at its branch: the portal offers the actions committed there, and syncs the clone again before each preview and run, so only what is on the branch counts. Listing a child also lets `toolbox serve` run it in that clone (`runners.local.portals`) unless `runners.local` is declared. Declares, unless already declared, the `federation` connector (builtin:workspace) and the `Portal` kind its records map to.

git.description: What `git clone` takes: a URL, or a path relative to this manifest's directory.

branch.description: The branch whose definitions count (default main).

key.description: The child's identity here: its entity is `portal:<key>` (default: the URL's last segment, without `.git`). Its manifest is `.toolbox/toolbox.yaml` in the repository.

permission.description: The relation a caller needs on the child portal entity to run its actions through this portal (default can_run_actions).

runner.description: How a parent may dispatch this portal's actions: `local` (the parent runs `toolbox run` in its clone of this repository), `ci` (the parent starts this repository's own CI on the forge it cloned it from: a GitLab pipeline, or a GitHub workflow), or `github-workflow` (the older GitHub-only form). The parent supplies the forge, project, API and token from where it cloned the child; a child never names them.

repo.description: github-workflow: owner/name of this portal's repository.

workflow.description: ci on GitHub and github-workflow: the workflow file that runs `toolbox run` (ci default toolbox.yml). GitLab runs the project's .gitlab-ci.yml.

ref.description: ci and github-workflow: the ref to run on (ci default: the branch the parent follows; github-workflow default main).

key.description: The parent's approval signing key, as `toolbox serve` prints it at start.

acceptApprovalsFrom.description: Parent portals whose signed approvals satisfy this portal's approval rules when they dispatch a run here. A grant counts only when its signature verifies with the pinned key and it names this run's action, version, inputs, effects and requester.

runners.description: A parent's runners: which children a server may run in its own process, and the credentials it dispatches workflows with. A served parent runs a child's actions only through a runner it declares here and the child declares in `runner`.

local.description: Children `toolbox serve` may run with `toolbox run` in its own checkout of them, as its own OS user.

portals.description: Child keys (the directory the workspace connector found each child in), `*` matching any run of characters.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the child beyond the base set (PATH, HOME, locale, proxies, git identity).

github-workflow.description: Workflows the parent may dispatch, and with which token.

repos.description: owner/name patterns a child's runner repo must match, `*` matching any run of characters.

token.description: The parent's environment variable holding the token (default GITHUB_TOKEN).

api.description: The API base URL (GitHub Enterprise Server or a test double).

signingKey.description: A parent's environment variable holding its approval signing key: 64 hex characters (32 random bytes, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`). Without it, a served parent can't pass approvals to its children.

package.description: builtin:<name> (shipped with toolbox), github:owner/repo[/app]@version (a released executable, installed by `toolbox install` and pinned in toolbox.lock, D90), or a path inside the image.

refresh.description: Refresh scopes the connector must declare at registration (connector-control §4).

description.description: What this means, for people and agents reading entities (shown by get and in the UI).

source.description: Source label for precedence; default connector:<connector>.

title.description: The name readers see (reports and the UI); defaults to the kind name split into words. Set it when two kinds would otherwise read alike.

description.description: What this means, for people and agents reading entities (shown by get and in the UI).

unresolved.description: Edges whose target is no entity are dropped; `report` (default) lists them as a derive diagnostic, `ignore` is for candidate relations (e.g. every code span that might name a tool).

title.description: A heading for people and agents; reports show it next to the name.

description.description: What the standard is and why: shown by reports and `toolbox describe`.

rationale.description: Why it matters: the outcome it protects or the failure it prevents, beyond what it checks and how to fix it. Reports show it beside the rule or scorecard.

links.description: Further reading behind it (decisions, design docs, outside sources).

track.description: Optional long-term program this scorecard belongs to (`tracks[].name`).

compare.description: Make this a comparative scorecard: score the subject and its peers on the same rules and report, per rule, whether the subject is ahead of, at parity with or behind each peer. Reports show the entities side by side.

subject.description: The entity the comparison is about (`product:toolbox`).

peers.description: The entities it is compared with (`product:backstage`).

verdict.description: How rule standings add up to the subject's standing per peer. `anyBehind`: behind if any rule is behind, then unknown, then ahead if any rule is ahead, else parity. `majority`: unknown if any rule is unknown, else ahead with more rules ahead than behind, behind with fewer, parity with as many. Use `majority` for an A/B whose tally was fixed before the run (D01M87WF2QZVPTD8CGDZKY133CD).

title.description: A short human name for the rule; reports show it before the name and otherwise spell the name out.

evidence.description: CEL evaluated when the rule fails: the items that make it fail (usually a list), shown with the fix and counted by `toolbox report` baselines.

measure.description: CEL evaluated when the rule fails: a number (lines in a file, occurrences of a pattern) that `toolbox report` baselines compare instead of the evidence count. Larger is worse; campaigns sum it to measure paydown.

value.description: CEL evaluated for every in-scope entity, pass or fail: the number a comparative scorecard compares (seconds, megabytes, a count). Reports show it beside the outcome. Requires `better`.

unit.description: The unit `value` is in, for reports (`s`, `MB`, `ms`, `packages`).

tolerance.description: Relative difference within which two values are at parity (0.1 = 10% of the larger magnitude). Default 0: only equal values are at parity.

rationale.description: Why it matters: the outcome it protects or the failure it prevents, beyond what it checks and how to fix it. Reports show it beside the rule or scorecard.

links.description: Further reading behind it (decisions, design docs, outside sources).

dataFrom.description: Connector this rule reads. Skipped, its missing data is an expected unknown and is not compared.

newEntitiesAtLeast.description: A level (or `none`) every entity new since the baseline must reach; below it is a regression, as new issues are in Betterer.

advisory.description: Report this scorecard but never gate on it: `toolbox report --baseline` leaves it out of the baseline and the comparison. For judgement-based scorecards (agent assessments), which go stale when their subject changes.

links.description: Further reading behind it (decisions, design docs, outside sources).

track.description: Optional track this campaign belongs to (`tracks[].name`).

targetPercent.description: Fleet goal: percent of in-scope entities that must meet every include (default 100).

draft.description: When true, status is draft regardless of dates.

status.description: Optional lifecycle override for fixtures and frozen reports.

atLeast.description: Entity level on this scorecard must be at least this level.

rules.description: Named rules that must pass on this scorecard.

entity.description: Entity id the waiver applies to.

decision.description: Decision file id. docs/decisions/<id>.md must exist.

scope.description: Where the action sits in its kind's lifecycle ([action-entities.md](../docs/design/action-entities.md)); default `day2`, an action on an existing entity.

inputs.description: JSON Schema for inputs; string properties may add enumFrom (CEL returning a list).

permission.description: OpenFGA relation checked on the target entity. Default `can_run_actions`.

command.description: in-image: the executor protocol v1 program; with package, the arguments the released binary gets.

package.description: in-image: a released executor, github:owner/repo[/app]@version, which toolbox install downloads and pins in toolbox.lock (D90), as it does connectors.

verify.description: in-image and http: the executor answers protocol verify with a read-back of the run's effect, which Toolbox asks for when the action declares no expect.

url.description: http: where Toolbox POSTs each protocol message and reads the replies (NDJSON or one JSON value). webhook: where it POSTs the protocol run message, and only its status counts.

secrets.description: command, change and in-image: environment variables the executor gets beyond the base set (PATH, HOME, locale, proxies, git identity). Executors start with a cleared environment.

oneOf.description: A shell line, run by sh -c.

run.description: command and change: what to run, from the directory toolbox started in (a change runs in a worktree of the base branch).

preview.description: command: the command supports TOOLBOX_PHASE=preview and prints its effects without changing anything.

base.description: change: the branch the change starts from and is verified on (default: the checked-out branch).

remote.description: change: the remote the branch is pushed to when it exists (default origin).

branch.description: change: the branch name; {action} and {run} are replaced (default toolbox/{action}/{run}). Inputs are not: they go only in message.

message.description: change: the commit message; {action}, {run}, {entity} and {inputs.<name>} are replaced, and toolbox validate refuses any other placeholder.

land.description: change: propose (default) pushes a branch for review, and review is the approval; push lands the commit on the base once the action's approval rule is met, never forced, and the run is done when the base is seen to have it.

review.description: change with land: propose: open a review for the branch on the remote's forge (default true): a merge request on GitLab (push options, no API token), a pull request on GitHub (with the forge's token). On plain git the pushed branch is the proposal.

project.description: gitlab-pipeline: the project path (group/subgroup/project). The forge comes from forges: (default https://gitlab.com).

forge.description: gitlab-pipeline: the forge's url, as forges: lists it (default https://gitlab.com).

ci.description: github-workflow and gitlab-pipeline: the ci: host (github-actions or gitlab-ci) whose endpoint and token to use, instead of forge, api and token.

ref.description: github-workflow and gitlab-pipeline: the ref to run on (default main).

api.description: github-workflow: the API base URL (GitHub Enterprise Server). gitlab-pipeline takes it from forges:.

token.description: github-workflow: the environment variable holding the token (default GITHUB_TOKEN). gitlab-pipeline takes it from forges:. http and webhook: the environment variable holding a bearer token (default: none sent).

unverified.description: Explicitly accept runs that can never be verified (action-runs §5).

context.description: Catalog lookups resolved at preview and run time and passed to the executor as `related`. `where` is CEL over `candidate`, `entity` and `inputs`.

link.description: Further reading: a decision, design doc or outside source. Reports link to it rather than repeat it.

url.description: An absolute http(s) URL, so it resolves wherever the report is hosted.
